title: OPS-23 P-168: dispatch preambles scoped by program; shared CANON-PREAMBLE fleet-wide only

missionPremise: Operator 2026-09-11 on the compiled P-151 dispatch: the preambles must cover the scope of what the program needs. Measured: nineteen of twenty-six CANON-PREAMBLE lines were Dashboards (G-xx) and Factory (F-xx) program law. The 2026-09-10 session measured the same (problem 6), recommended scoping the preamble by program, and did not row it.
completionPredicate: An OPS-23 dispatch compiled with no flag carries the fleet-wide bullets plus the OPS-23 program preamble and zero Dashboards rows; a shared bullet naming a plan row is refused at state regeneration; a row inside a registered program refuses to compile when its program file is missing; a row outside any program compiles with no program context.
scopeBasis: Data move plus two controls, no change to the canon gate: the gate validates rows and the CANON-PREAMBLE hash, both of which keep working unchanged (the hash simply moves to the trimmed body). The registry `programs` block is read by the compiler only, which the divergence test tolerates (16 of 16).

lessonsForFleetMemory: A preamble that carries everything teaches lanes to skim it; scope is what makes a preamble readable, and scope has to be enforced at the generator or it decays in a week.
Verify a control through the process that calls it: both new controls here were exercised by running the generator and the compiler, not by unit tests alone.
